The leader changes the follower’s choices.

A Primal-Dual-Assisted Penalty Approach to Bilevel Optimization with Coupled Constraints

Liuyuan Jiang, Quan Xiao, Victor M. Tenorio, Fernando Real-Rojas, Antonio G. Marques, Tianyi Chen

Project pageRead the paper

Ready to recordNarration and storyboard draft

~2 minutesFive scenes with diagram pauses

Recorded video will be added here when available.

0:00–0:20

Some decisions change what other decision-makers are allowed to do. A network design determines which routes users can choose. This is a natural bilevel problem with coupled constraints.

On screen: Show an operator changing a network, then users selecting routes.

0:20–0:45

The outer variable changes the inner feasible set. We need to account for a moving boundary, including cases where the lower-level optimum lies on that boundary.

On screen: Move the bound y≤xy\leq xy≤x and the constrained optimum in the toy example.

0:45–1:10

BLOCC uses a primal-dual-assisted penalty formulation. Dual information captures the role of lower-level constraints, while the algorithm uses first-order updates.

On screen: Add primal variables and dual multipliers to a constraint box.

1:10–1:35

The approximation and convergence results rely on a specific regime: a strongly convex lower-level objective, convex lower-level constraints, feasible domains, and the stated regularity conditions.

On screen: Display the lower-level strong convexity, constraint convexity, and regularity assumptions.

1:35–2:00

The experiments study constrained SVM hyperparameter optimization and transportation planning. The takeaway is to model the changing feasible set explicitly when the outer decision reshapes the inner problem.

On screen: Show SVM and Seville transportation headings from Section 4.
